stories.headline: Powerful 7.7 earthquake strikes eastern Indonesia
stories.summary: A shallow 7.7-magnitude earthquake hit Indonesia's Flores region early Saturday, with BBC reporting at least 38 deaths and rescue teams searching for survivors. Al Jazeera reported the death toll was expected to rise as thousands sought higher ground and emergency crews continued their work.
stories.pastoral_note: A morning to pray Psalm 46 with trembling honesty: God is refuge when the earth literally gives way. Consider leading intercession for grieving families, rescue workers, and churches serving as shelter and comfort.

stories.headline: At least 31 Christians killed in attacks in central Nigeria
stories.summary: Christian News Network, citing Christian Daily International-Morning Star News, reported that Fulani herdsmen killed at least 31 Christians across central Nigeria, including 16 in Plateau state since Aug. 2 and additional deaths in Nasarawa and Benue states.
stories.pastoral_note: This is not abstract geopolitics; these are members of Christ's body. Hold together lament, advocacy, and hope: 'If one member suffers, all suffer together' (1 Cor. 12:26).

stories.headline: France's top court blocks under-15 social media ban
stories.summary: BBC reports France's Constitutional Council struck down a planned social media ban for children under 15, ruling it was not proportionate to freedom of expression and lacked adequate safeguards around age verification. President Macron has asked for a revised draft.
stories.pastoral_note: The culture is naming the harm of digital life but struggling to agree on wise limits. This is a discipleship opening: families need practices, not just policies, for attention, embodiment, and holiness.

stories.headline: Landmark jury holds Instagram and YouTube liable in social media addiction case
stories.summary: AP reports a California jury found Meta and YouTube liable for designing platforms that hooked young users without sufficient concern for wellbeing, awarding millions to a plaintiff who said childhood social media addiction worsened her mental health struggles.
stories.pastoral_note: This presses an old Christian question in a new form: what is forming our loves? Pastors can speak with clarity about human dignity without panic, helping parents and youth recover agency before the algorithm.

stories.headline: HBR: Organizations decide whom they trust before CEO selection begins
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review's latest leadership page features 'Why Lateral Hires Rarely Become CEO,' arguing that institutions form collective judgments about who can represent them long before boards make formal choices.
stories.pastoral_note: Leadership credibility is accumulated, not announced. In church life, this is a reminder to develop trustworthy people slowly, visibly, and relationally before urgent succession moments arrive.

stories.headline: Lower Mainland housing remains in buyers' market territory
stories.summary: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board says July remained firmly in buyers' territory, with benchmark prices down 7% year over year and 1,089 homes sold. WOWA reports Metro Vancouver's July benchmark price was $1,088,800, down 6.2% annually, with about eight months of supply.
stories.pastoral_note: Falling prices do not automatically mean affordability for young families. This remains a pastoral pressure point: housing anxiety shapes generosity, vocation, marriage, and whether people feel rooted in community.

stories.headline: American missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine months
stories.summary: The Guardian reports American missionary Kevin Rideout, abducted in Niamey nine months ago, has been freed and is said to be in good health and in the care of U.S. officials.
stories.pastoral_note: A sober mercy worth giving thanks for. This kind of story can help a congregation practice both persistent prayer and grateful testimony without forgetting others still captive or endangered.

stories.headline: Texas barbecue gets a halal makeover amid rising anti-Muslim rhetoric
stories.summary: Religion News Service reports Muslim pitmasters in Fort Worth are reshaping Texas barbecue with halal offerings, winning over diners while anti-Muslim rhetoric rises in the state.
stories.pastoral_note: Food remains one of the most ordinary places where strangers become neighbors. For evangelistic imagination, this is a table-fellowship moment: Christians can practice convictional hospitality rather than culture-war reflexes.
